_comment: Every place stipend.sh is published, and how each one is updated.
Seeded from the lister's submission ledger on 17 August 2026.
'push' is what publish.py can do unattended. 'manual' needs a human in a
browser or a passkey. 'static' means the listing carries no version or
changing content, so a release does not make it stale - most awesome-list
entries are a name, a line of description and a URL, and re-opening forty
pull requests for a patch bump would be spam.
Anything listed here as 'stale_on_release' is what a release must reach.

push.name: stipend.sh (our own site)
push.why_it_matters: install.py and every directory's docs link point here

manual.name: npm
manual.holds: a shim that downloads install.py — no client code
manual.note: Version number only. The shim always fetches the live tarball, so npm users get the new client without a republish. Bump for tidiness, not correctness.
manual.how: npm publish (Matt's passkey — he enters it himself)

manual.name: ClawHub
manual.holds: an uploaded folder including SKILL.md with a pinned version
manual.how: browser upload; GitHub import never worked (could not see the org)

manual.name: Claw Mart
manual.holds: package v3, uploaded 14 Aug, plus the about text
manual.note: Their security scan rejects curl|sh. Keep install notes on npx.

manual.name: glama.ai
manual.holds: reads glama.json and the README from the repo
manual.how: re-scans the repo on its own schedule

static.name: awesome-list pull requests
static.note: Each carries a name, one line and a URL. A version bump does not make them wrong. Re-open only if the description or the URL changes.

static.name: x402 and agent directories
static.note: They index endpoints and descriptions, not client versions. agent-tools.cloud and 402directory.com publish no update route at all; x402-list.com has /services/{slug}/request-update once a listing is public.

static.name: llms.txt directories
static.note: They fetch https://stipend.sh/llms.txt live, so publishing the site is the update.
